translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, acting on his own authority, left all local officials in place as Shichong had appointed them and renamed Yu Prefecture Southern Bian Prefecture; Henan's prefectures and counties then defected one after another.

sentences.zh: 劉武周降將尋相等多叛去。

translations.literal: Many surrendered generals of Liu Wuzhou such as Xun Xiang rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Liu Wuzhou's surrendered generals, including Xun Xiang, broke away and deserted.

sentences.zh: 諸將疑尉遲敬德，囚之軍中。

translations.literal: The generals suspected Yuchi Jingde and imprisoned him in the army.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders grew suspicious of Yuchi Jingde and had him imprisoned in camp.

sentences.zh: 行臺左僕射屈突通、尚書殷開山言於世民曰：「敬德驍勇絕倫，今既囚之，心必怨望，留之恐為後患，不如遂殺之。

translations.literal: Campaign Headquarters Left Vice Minister Qu Tu Tong and Minister Yin Kaishan said to Shimin, "Jingde's martial valor is unmatched. Now that he is imprisoned, he must harbor resentment; keeping him may become a future threat—it would be better to kill him at once."
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Tong, Left Vice Minister of the campaign headquarters, and Minister Yin Kaishan urged Shimin, "Jingde's courage is unmatched. Imprisoned now, he will only grow resentful. Keeping him is a risk—it would be safer to kill him."

sentences.zh: 」世民曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Shimin said, "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: " Shimin said, "No."

sentences.zh: 敬德若叛，豈在尋相之後邪！

translations.literal: If Jingde were to rebel, would he wait until after Xun Xiang!
translations.idiomatic: If Jingde meant to rebel, he would not still be here after Xun Xiang already went!

sentences.zh: 」遽命釋之，引入臥內，賜之金，曰：「丈夫意氣相期，勿以小嫌介意，吾終不信讒言以害忠良，公宜體之。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered him released, brought him into his private chamber, bestowed gold upon him, and said, "Men of honor pledge their loyalty to one another—do not let a small grievance rankle. I will never believe slander to harm the loyal and worthy; you should understand this."
translations.idiomatic: " He had Jingde released at once and brought him into his private quarters, presenting him with gold. "Men of honor trust one another," he said. "Do not let a petty grievance come between us. I will never believe slander against the loyal—you should know that."

sentences.zh: 必欲去者，以此金相資，表一時共事之情也。

translations.literal: If you must leave, use this gold as travel funds—it expresses the affection of our time serving together."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to go, take this gold as my parting gift—a token of what we shared."

sentences.zh: 」辛巳，世民以五百騎行戰地，登魏宣武陵。

translations.literal: " On the day xinsi, Shimin rode five hundred cavalry over the battlefield and ascended the tomb-mound of Emperor Xuanwu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day xinsi, Shimin rode out with five hundred cavalry to survey the field and climbed the mound of Emperor Xuanwu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 王世充帥步騎萬餘猝至，圍之。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry and suddenly arrived, surrounding him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong appeared suddenly with more than ten thousand foot and horse and surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 單雄信引槊直趨世民，敬德躍馬大呼，橫刺雄信墜馬，世充兵稍卻，敬德翼世民出圍。

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin levelled his spear and charged straight at Shimin; Jingde leapt on his horse with a great shout and thrust horizontally, knocking Xiongxin from his horse; Shichong's troops fell back slightly; Jingde shielded Shimin and escorted him out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin drove his spear straight at Shimin. Yuchi Jingde spurred forward with a roar and struck Xiongxin from the saddle. Shichong's line buckled; Jingde shepherded Shimin out of the trap.

sentences.zh: 世民、敬德更帥騎兵還戰，出入世充陳，往返無所礙。

translations.literal: Shimin and Jingde then led cavalry back to fight, passing in and out of Shichong's battle line without hindrance going or returning.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin and Jingde wheeled about with their cavalry, charging through Shichong's ranks as if the enemy line were open ground.

sentences.zh: 屈突通引大兵繼至，世充兵大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Qu Tu Tong brought up the main force in support; Shichong's troops were utterly defeated, and he barely escaped with his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Tong arrived with the main body; Shichong's army collapsed, and he barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 擒其冠軍大將軍陳智略，斬首千餘級，獲排槊兵六千。

translations.literal: They captured his Champion Grand General Chen Zhilüe, took more than a thousand heads, and seized six thousand pike soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Tang captured Champion Grand General Chen Zhilüe, took over a thousand heads, and took six thousand pike infantry prisoner.

sentences.zh: 世民謂敬德曰：「公何相報之速也！

translations.literal: Shimin said to Jingde, "How quickly you repaid my trust!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin told Jingde, "You repaid my trust quickly!"

sentences.zh: 」賜敬德金銀一篋，自是寵遇日隆。

translations.literal: " He bestowed on Jingde a casket of gold and silver; from this time favor toward him grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave Jingde a chest of gold and silver; from then on Jingde's favor at court only grew.

sentences.zh: 敬德善避槊，每單騎入敵陳中，敵叢槊刺之，終莫能傷，又能奪敵槊返剌之。

translations.literal: Jingde was skilled at evading spears; whenever he rode alone into the enemy battle line and the enemy thrust at him in clusters with spears, in the end none could wound him; he could also snatch the enemy's spears and turn them back in thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde had a gift for dodging spears. Riding alone into enemy lines, he could weather a storm of thrusts unscathed—and seize a spear from his assailants and stab them with it.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉以善馬槊自負，聞敬德之能，請各去刃相與校勝負，敬德曰：「敬德謹當去之，王勿去也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Yuanji, prided himself on skill with horse and spear; hearing of Jingde's ability, he requested that each remove the blade and spar to determine the victor; Jingde said, "Jingde will respectfully remove his blade—Your Highness need not remove yours."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanji of Qi, proud of his lance-work, heard of Jingde's skill and proposed a bout with blunted weapons. Jingde said, "I'll take the edge off my lance, Your Highness—yours can stay sharp."

sentences.zh: 」既而元吉刺之，終不能中。

translations.literal: " Then Yuanji thrust at him but to the end could not hit him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanji struck again and again but never touched him.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民問敬德曰：「避槊與奪槊，孰難？

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Shimin, asked Jingde, "Evading a spear and seizing a spear—which is harder?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin asked Jingde, "Which is harder—dodging a spear or taking one away?"

sentences.zh: 」敬德曰：「奪槊難。

translations.literal: " Jingde said, "Seizing a spear is harder."
translations.idiomatic: " "Taking one is harder," Jingde said.

sentences.zh: 」乃命敬德奪元吉槊。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Jingde to seize Yuanji's spear.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince ordered Jingde to disarm Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 元吉操槊躍馬，志在刺之，敬德須臾三奪其槊；

translations.literal: Yuanji grasped his spear and leapt on his horse, intent on stabbing him; in a brief moment Jingde thrice seized his spear;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji spurred forward, spear raised to strike—but in moments Jingde snatched it from his hands three times;

sentences.zh: 元吉雖面相歎異，內甚恥之。

translations.literal: Although Yuanji's face showed wonder and admiration, inwardly he was deeply shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji marveled aloud, but inside he burned with humiliation.

sentences.zh: 叛胡陷嵐州。

translations.literal: Rebellious Hu tribes captured Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious Hu tribes overran Lan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，王世充以邴元真為滑州行臺僕射。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Shichong had appointed Bing Yuanzhen Vice Minister of the Hua Prefecture Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Shichong had made Bing Yuanzhen vice minister of the Hua Prefecture campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 濮州刺史杜才幹，李密故將也，恨元真叛密，詐以其眾降之。

translations.literal: Puzhou Prefect Du Caigan, a former general of Li Mi, hated Yuanzhen for betraying Mi and feigned surrender of his force to him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Caigan, prefect of Pu Prefecture and a former Li Mi commander, despised Yuanzhen for betraying Mi and pretended to surrender his troops to him.

sentences.zh: 元真恃其官勢，自往招慰，才幹出迎，延入就坐，執而數之曰：「汝本庸才，魏化置汝元僚，不建毫髮之功，乃構滔天之禍，今來送死，是汝之分！

translations.literal: Yuanzhen relied on his official authority and went in person to win them over; Caigan went out to welcome him, invited him in to be seated, seized him and berated him, saying, "You were originally a mediocrity; the Duke of Wei placed you among his chief ministers, yet you achieved not the slightest merit and instead brought about heaven-reaching calamity. Now you have come to deliver yourself to death—that is your appointed portion!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen, confident in his rank, went personally to accept the surrender. Caigan welcomed him, seated him—and seized him. "You were a nobody," he raged. "The Duke of Wei made you one of his chief ministers, and you repaid him with treason that brought ruin on us all. You came here to die—that is your fate."

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之，遣人繼其首至黎陽祭密墓。

translations.literal: " He then beheaded him and sent men to carry the head in succession to Liyang to offer sacrifice at Mi's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Yuanzhen beheaded and sent his head to Liyang to be offered before Li Mi's grave.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以濮州來降。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, he surrendered Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, Pu Prefecture came over to Tang.

sentences.zh: 突厥莫賀咄設寇涼州，總管楊恭仁擊之，為所敗，掠男女數千人而去。

translations.literal: The Turkic Mohuad she raided Liang Prefecture; Commander Yang Gongren struck at them, was defeated by them, and they carried off several thousand men and women and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Mohuad she raided Liang Prefecture. Commander Yang Gongren gave battle and was routed; the raiders carried off several thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以田瓚為顯州總管，賜爵蔡國公。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Tian Zan was appointed Xianzhou Commander and granted the title Duke of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu, Tian Zan was made commander of Xian Prefecture and created Duke of Cai.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲午，王世充大將軍張鎮周來降。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiawu, Wang Shichong's Grand General Zhang Zhenzhou came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jiawu, Zhang Zhenzhou, a grand general under Wang Shichong, defected.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，行軍總管羅士信襲王世充硤石堡，拔之。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Campaign Commander Luo Shixin raided Wang Shichong's Xiashi Fort and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen, Campaign Commander Luo Shixin stormed Wang Shichong's Xiashi Fort and took it.

sentences.zh: 士信又圍千金堡，堡中人罵之。

translations.literal: Shixin again besieged Qianjin Fort; the men in the fort cursed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin next invested Qianjin Fort; its defenders hurled abuse at him.

sentences.zh: 士信夜遣百餘人抱嬰兒數十至堡下，使兒啼呼，詐云「從東都來歸羅總管」。

translations.literal: Shixin by night sent more than a hundred men carrying several dozen infants to the foot of the fort, making the children wail and cry, falsely claiming, "We have come from the Eastern Capital to surrender to Commander Luo."
translations.idiomatic: Shixin sent more than a hundred men at night with dozens of wailing infants to the fort gate, crying out that they were refugees from the Eastern Capital coming to surrender to Commander Luo.

sentences.zh: 既而相謂曰：「此千金堡也，吾屬誤矣。

translations.literal: Then they said to one another, "This is Qianjin Fort—we have made a mistake."
translations.idiomatic: Then they called to one another, "This is Qianjin Fort—we've come to the wrong place."

sentences.zh: 」即去。

translations.literal: They left at once.
translations.idiomatic: They left at once.

sentences.zh: 堡中以為士信已去，來者洛陽亡人，出兵追之。

translations.literal: The fort thought Shixin had already gone and that those who came were refugees fleeing Luoyang; they sent troops out in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The fort's garrison assumed Shixin had withdrawn and that these were Luoyang refugees, and sallied out in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 士信伏兵於道，伺其門開，突入，屠之。

translations.literal: Shixin had hidden troops along the road; when the gate opened he waited for the chance, burst in, and slaughtered them.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin had men hidden along the road; when the gates opened, his troops poured in and massacred the garrison.

sentences.zh: 竇建德之圍幽州也，李藝告急於高開道，開道帥二千騎救之，建德兵引去，開道因藝遣使來降。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande was besieging Youzhou, Li Yi urgently appealed to Gao Kaidao; Kaidao led two thousand cavalry to rescue him; Jiande's troops withdrew; Kaidao then through Yi sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While Dou Jiande besieged Youzhou, Li Yi urgently called on Gao Kaidao, who rode to the rescue with two thousand cavalry. Jiande withdrew, and Kaidao sent envoys through Li Yi to submit to Tang.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以開道為蔚州總管，賜姓李氏，封北平郡王。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Kaidao was appointed Weizhou Commander, granted the surname Li, and enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen, Kaidao was made commander of Wei Prefecture, given the imperial surname Li, and created Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 開道有矢鏃在頰，召醫出之，醫曰：「鏃深，不可出。

translations.literal: Kaidao had an arrowhead lodged in his cheek; he summoned a physician to extract it; the physician said, "The arrowhead is deep—it cannot be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao had an arrowhead embedded in his cheek and summoned a physician. "It is too deep," the doctor said. "It cannot come out."

sentences.zh: 」開道怒，斬之。

translations.literal: " Kaidao grew angry and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " Kaidao had him beheaded in a rage.

sentences.zh: 別召一醫，曰：「出之恐痛。

translations.literal: He summoned another physician, who said, "Extracting it will probably hurt."
translations.idiomatic: He called in another physician. "It will hurt to remove it," the man warned.

sentences.zh: 」又斬之。

translations.literal: " He beheaded him as well.
translations.idiomatic: " Kaidao killed him too.

sentences.zh: 更召一醫，醫曰：「可出。

translations.literal: He summoned yet another physician; the physician said, "It can be removed."
translations.idiomatic: A third physician was brought. "It can be removed," he said.

sentences.zh: 」乃鑿骨，置楔其間，骨裂寸餘，竟出其鏃；

translations.literal: " He then chiseled the bone, inserted a wedge between, the bone cracked more than an inch, and finally the arrowhead was extracted;
translations.idiomatic: " He chiseled through the bone, wedged it apart an inch or more, and at last pulled out the arrowhead;

sentences.zh: 開道奏妓進膳不輟。

translations.literal: Kaidao had musicians perform and meals served without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the ordeal, Kaidao kept musicians playing and food coming without pause.

sentences.zh: 竇建德帥眾二十萬復攻幽州。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande led two hundred thousand troops to attack Youzhou again.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande returned with two hundred thousand men to assault Youzhou again.

sentences.zh: 建德兵已攀堞，薛萬均、薛萬徹帥敢死士百人從地道出其背，掩擊之，建德兵潰走，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Jiande's troops had already scaled the battlements; Xue Wanjun and Xue Wanche led a hundred dare-to-die soldiers through a tunnel to emerge behind them and strike by surprise; Jiande's troops collapsed and fled; more than a thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's men had already reached the battlements when Xue Wanjun and Xue Wanche led a hundred dare-to-die soldiers through a tunnel to strike from behind. Jiande's army broke and fled, leaving over a thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 李藝兵乘勝薄其營，建德陳於營中，填塹而出，奮擊，大破之，建德逐北。

translations.literal: Li Yi's troops, riding the victory, pressed close to the camp; Jiande formed his line within the camp, filled the moat and sallied forth, fought fiercely, suffered a great defeat, and fled northward in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi's forces pressed the attack on Jiande's camp. Jiande formed up within his lines, filled the moats, and sallied forth—but Li Yi broke him completely and drove him north in flight.

sentences.zh: 至其城下，攻之，不克而還。

translations.literal: They reached the walls of his city, attacked it, failed to capture it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued to Jiande's city walls, assaulted it without success, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李密之敗也，楊慶歸洛陽，復姓楊氏。

translations.literal: When Li Mi was defeated, Yang Qing returned to Luoyang and restored the surname Yang.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi's defeat, Yang Qing went back to Luoyang and resumed the Yang surname.

sentences.zh: 及王世充稱帝，慶復姓郭氏，世充以為管州總管，妻以兄女。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, Qing again took the surname Guo; Shichong appointed him Guan Prefecture commander and gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong declared himself emperor, Qing took the Guo surname again; Shichong made him commander of Guan Prefecture and married him to his niece.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民逼洛陽，慶潛遣人請降，世民遣總管李世勣將兵往據其城。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Shimin, pressed Luoyang; Qing secretly sent men to request surrender; Shimin dispatched Commander Li Shiji to lead troops to occupy his city.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Qin tightened the siege of Luoyang, Qing secretly sent envoys to offer surrender; Shimin sent Li Shiji to occupy Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 慶欲與其妻偕來，妻曰：「主上使妾侍巾櫛者，欲結君之心也。

translations.literal: Qing wished to come together with his wife; his wife said, "The sovereign sent me to attend your comb and toilet because he wished to win your heart."
translations.idiomatic: Qing wanted his wife to come with him. She said, "Our lord gave me to you to bind your loyalty."

sentences.zh: 今君既辜付託，徇利求全，妾將如君何！

translations.literal: Now that you have betrayed that trust, seeking profit and preserving yourself whole—what am I to do with you!"
translations.idiomatic: "Now you break that trust for safety and gain—what am I to do with you?"

sentences.zh: 若至長安，則君家一婢耳，君何用為！

translations.literal: If we reach Chang'an, I will be but a maidservant in your house—of what use will you be to me!"
translations.idiomatic: "In Chang'an I would be nothing but a servant in your household—what good would you be to me then?"

sentences.zh: 願送至洛陽，君之惠也。

translations.literal: I wish to be sent back to Luoyang—that would be your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: "Send me back to Luoyang—that is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 」慶不許。

translations.literal: " Qing did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing refused.

sentences.zh: 慶出，妻謂侍者曰：「若唐遂勝鄭，則吾家必滅；

translations.literal: When Qing went out, his wife said to the attendants, "If Tang in the end defeats Zheng, then our family will surely be destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: After Qing left, his wife told her attendants, "If Tang wins over Zheng, our house will be destroyed;

sentences.zh: 鄭若勝唐，則吾夫必死。

translations.literal: if Zheng defeats Tang, then my husband will surely die."
translations.idiomatic: if Zheng wins, my husband will die."

sentences.zh: 人生至此，何用生為！

translations.literal: Life reaching this point—what use is living!"
translations.idiomatic: "Life has come to this—why go on living?"

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: " She thereupon killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She took her own life.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，慶來降，復姓楊氏，拜上柱國、郇國公。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Qing came to surrender, restored the surname Yang, and was appointed Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Qing surrendered, took back the Yang surname, and was created Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 時世充太子玄應鎮虎牢，軍於宋、汴之間，聞之，引兵趣管城，李世勣擊卻之。

translations.literal: At that time Shichong's crown prince Xuanying was garrisoning Hulao with troops between Song and Bian; hearing of this, he led troops toward Guancheng; Li Shiji repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xuanying was then at Hulao with forces between Song and Bian; when he heard the news he marched on Guancheng, but Li Shiji drove him back.

sentences.zh: 使郭孝恪為書說榮州刺史魏陸，陸密請降。

translations.literal: He had Guo Xiaoke write a letter to persuade Rong Prefecture governor Wei Lu; Lu secretly requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin had Guo Xiaoke write to Rong Prefecture Governor Wei Lu, who secretly offered to defect.

sentences.zh: 玄應遣大將軍張志就陸徵兵，丙辰，陸擒志等四將，舉州來降。

translations.literal: Xuanying sent Grand General Zhang Zhi to Lu to levy troops; on the day bingchen, Lu captured Zhi and three other generals and surrendered the entire prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanying sent Grand General Zhang Zhi to Lu to raise troops; on the day bingchen, Lu seized Zhang Zhi and three other generals and brought the whole prefecture over.

sentences.zh: 陽城令王雄帥諸堡來降，秦王世民使李世勣引兵應之，以雄為嵩州刺史，嵩南之路始通。

translations.literal: Yangcheng magistrate Wang Xiong led the various forts to surrender; the Prince of Qin, Shimin, sent Li Shiji to lead troops to meet him; Wang Xiong was appointed Song Prefecture governor, and the route south of Song was opened for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong, magistrate of Yangcheng, brought over the surrounding forts; the Prince of Qin sent Li Shiji to meet him and made Wang Xiong governor of Song Prefecture, opening the route south of Mount Song for the first time.

sentences.zh: 魏陸使張志詐為玄應書，停其東道之兵，令其將張慈寶且還汴州，又密告汴州刺史王要漢使圖慈寶，要漢斬慈寶以降。

translations.literal: Wei Lu had Zhang Zhi forge a letter in Xuanying's name, halting the eastern-route troops and ordering his general Zhang Cibao to return temporarily to Bian Prefecture; he also secretly told Bian Prefecture governor Wang Yaohan to plot against Cibao—Yaohan beheaded Cibao and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lu had Zhang Zhi forge a dispatch in Xuanying's name, ordering the eastern army to stand down and sending General Zhang Cibao back to Bian Prefecture for the moment. In secret he also urged Bian's governor Wang Yaohan to eliminate Cibao; Yaohan cut off Cibao's head and defected.

sentences.zh: 玄應聞諸州皆叛，大懼，奔還洛陽。

translations.literal: Xuanying heard that all the prefectures were rebelling; greatly alarmed, he fled back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanying learned that prefecture after prefecture was turning against him, he was terrified and raced back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔以要漢為汴州總管，賜爵郳國公。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yaohan commander of Bian Prefecture and ennobled him as Duke of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Yaohan commander of Bian Prefecture and created him Duke of Bi.

sentences.zh: 王弘烈據襄陽，上令金州總管府司馬涇陽李大亮安撫樊、鄧以圖之。

translations.literal: Wang Honglie held Xiangyang; the Emperor ordered Li Daliang of Jingyang, adjutant of the Jin Prefecture command headquarters, to pacify Fan and Deng and scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Honglie still held Xiangyang. The Emperor sent Li Daliang of Jingyang, adjutant on the Jin Prefecture staff, to win over Fan and Deng and lay plans against him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚申，大亮攻樊城鎮，拔之，斬其將國大安，下其城柵十四。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day gengshen, Daliang attacked Fancheng garrison, took it, beheaded its commander Guo Da'an, and captured fourteen walled camps below the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day gengshen, Daliang stormed Fancheng garrison, killed its commander Guo Da'an, and reduced fourteen outlying camps.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑性褊狹，多猜忌。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian was narrow-minded by nature and deeply suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian was petty by temperament and quick to suspect those around him.

sentences.zh: 諸將恃功恣橫，好專誅殺，銑患之，乃宣言罷兵營農，實欲奪諸將之權。

translations.literal: The generals, relying on merit, acted lawlessly and were given to arbitrary executions; Xian worried over this, proclaimed disbanding the army and turning to farming, but in fact meant to strip the generals of power.
translations.idiomatic: His generals, bloated with pride in their victories, ran wild and killed at whim. Xian hated it. He announced that the armies would be stood down and sent to the fields—but his real aim was to wrest power from the commanders.

sentences.zh: 大司馬董景珍弟為將軍，怨望，謀作亂；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Dong Jingzhen's younger brother, a general, nursed resentment and plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jingzhen's younger brother, a general serving as grand marshal, brooded over his grievances and plotted revolt;

sentences.zh: 事洩，伏誅。

translations.literal: When the affair leaked out, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 景珍時鎮長沙，銑下詔赦之，召還江陵。

translations.literal: Jingzhen was then stationed at Changsha; Xian issued an edict pardoning him and summoned him back to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen was then holding Changsha. Xian issued a pardon and ordered him back to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 景珍懼，甲子，以長沙來降；

translations.literal: Jingzhen was afraid; on the day jiazi he surrendered Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Jingzhen surrendered Changsha on the day jiazi;

sentences.zh: 詔峽州刺史許紹出兵應之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xia Prefecture governor Xu Shao to march out in support.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xu Shao, governor of Xia Prefecture, to move troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 雲州總管郭子和，先與突厥、梁師都相連結，既而襲師都寧朔城，克之。

translations.literal: Yun Prefecture commander Guo Zihe had first been allied with the Turks and Liang Shidu; afterward he attacked Shidu's Ningshuo fortress and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zihe, commander of Yun Prefecture, had first thrown in his lot with the Turks and Liang Shidu—then turned and stormed Shidu's fortress at Ningshuo.

sentences.zh: 又得突厥釁隙，遣使以聞，為突厥候騎所獲。

translations.literal: He also found grounds for quarrel with the Turks and sent an envoy to report it, but Turkish scouts captured the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: He picked a quarrel with the Turks as well and sent word to the court—but Turkish scouts intercepted his messenger.

sentences.zh: 處羅可汗大怒，囚其弟子升。

translations.literal: Khan Quluo was furious and imprisoned Zihe's nephew Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Quluo flew into a rage and clapped Zihe's nephew Sheng in irons.

sentences.zh: 子和自以孤危，請帥其民南徙，詔以延州故城處之。

translations.literal: Zihe, feeling isolated and imperiled, asked to lead his people south to relocate; an edict settled them at the old site of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling exposed and alone, Zihe asked leave to lead his people south. The court granted them the abandoned city of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張舉、劉旻之降也，梁師都大懼，遣其尚書陸季覽說突厥處羅可汗曰：「比者中原喪亂，分為數國，勢均力弱，故皆北面歸附突厥。

translations.literal: When Zhang Ju and Liu Min surrendered, Liang Shidu was greatly alarmed and sent his minister of the interior Lu Jilan to persuade Turkish Khan Quluo, saying, "Recently the central plains have fallen into chaos and split into several states, all weak and evenly matched, so each turned north to submit to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ju and Liu Min defected, Liang Shidu was terrified. He sent his minister Lu Jilan to urge Khan Quluo of the Turks: "While the heartland has been torn apart, every petty realm was too weak to stand alone—so all bowed north to you.

sentences.zh: 今定楊可汗既亡，天下將悉為唐有。

translations.literal: Now that Dingyang Khan is dead, soon all the realm will belong to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Now Dingyang Khan is gone, and before long all under heaven will belong to Tang.

sentences.zh: 師都不辭灰滅，亦恐次及可汗。

translations.literal: Shidu will not shrink from being ground to ashes—but I fear you, Khan, will be next.
translations.idiomatic: I do not flinch from my own ruin—but I fear, Khan, that you will be next.

sentences.zh: 不若及其未定，南取中原，如魏道武所為，師都請為鄉導。

translations.literal: Better, while their order is not yet settled, to march south and seize the central plains, as Emperor Daowu of Wei did; Shidu offers to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Better strike while they are still unsettled—march south and take the central plains, as Emperor Daowu of Wei once did. Shidu will guide you.

sentences.zh: 」處羅從之，謀使莫賀咄設入自原州，泥步設與師都入自延州，處羅入自并州，突利可汗與奚、□、契丹、靺鞨入自幽州，會竇建德之師自滏口西入，會於晉、絳。

translations.literal: Quluo agreed and planned to have Moheduo She enter from Yuan Prefecture, Nibu She and Shidu enter from Yan Prefecture, Quluo enter from Bing Prefecture, Khan Tuli with the Xi, Xi, Khitans, and Mohe enter from You Prefecture, and to meet Dou Jiande's army entering west from Fukou, converging at Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Quluo agreed. He planned for Moheduo She to enter from Yuan Prefecture, Nibu She and Shidu from Yan, Quluo himself from Bing, Khan Tuli with the Xi, Khitans, and Mohe from You, and Dou Jiande's army from Fukou in the west—all to rendezvous in Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄者，處羅之弟咄苾也；

translations.literal: Moheduo was Quluo's younger brother Tubo;
translations.idiomatic: Moheduo was Quluo's younger brother Tubo;

sentences.zh: 突利者，始畢之子什缽苾也。

translations.literal: Tuli was Shibi's son Shibobi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli was Shibobi, son of the late Khan Shibi.

sentences.zh: 處羅又欲取并州以居楊政道，其群臣多諫，處羅曰：「我父失國，賴隋得立，此恩不可忘！

translations.literal: Quluo also wanted to take Bing Prefecture to install Yang Zhengdao; many of his ministers remonstrated. Quluo said, "When my father lost his state, we relied on Sui to be established—this debt must not be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: Quluo also meant to seize Bing Prefecture and install Yang Zhengdao there. Many of his ministers objected. Quluo said, "My father lost his throne; only Sui restored us— that debt cannot be forgotten!

sentences.zh: 」將出師而卒。

translations.literal: He was about to march out when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the point of marching when he died.

sentences.zh: 義成公主以其子奧射設丑弱，廢之，更立莫賀咄設，號頡利可汗。

translations.literal: Princess Yicheng, finding her son Aoshe weak and worthless, deposed him and instead installed Moheduo She as khan, styled Il khan.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yicheng judged her son Aoshe feeble and unfit, set him aside, and raised Moheduo She instead as khan, styled Il.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，頡利遣使告處羅之喪，上禮之如始畢之喪。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Il sent envoys to announce Quluo's death; the Emperor received them with the same ceremonial mourning as for Shibi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, Il sent envoys to announce Quluo's death. The Emperor received them with the same state mourning he had shown at Shibi's passing.

sentences.zh: 戊子，安撫大使李大亮取王世充沮、華二州。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, pacification commissioner Li Daliang took Wang Shichong's Qu and Hua prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi, Pacification Commissioner Li Daliang seized Qu and Hua, two prefectures held by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 是月，竇建德濟河擊孟海公。

translations.literal: That month, Dou Jiande crossed the river and attacked Meng Haigong.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Dou Jiande crossed the Yellow River to strike Meng Haigong.

sentences.zh: 初，王世充侵建德黎陽，建德襲破殷州以報之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Shichong had invaded Jiande's Liyang, Jiande had raided and smashed Yin Prefecture in retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Shichong had invaded Jiande's territory at Liyang; Jiande had answered by storming Yin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自是二國交惡，信使不通。

translations.literal: From then on the two states were estranged and envoys no longer passed between them.
translations.idiomatic: After that the two realms were bitter enemies and no envoy crossed between them.

sentences.zh: 及唐兵逼洛陽，世充遣使求救於建德。

translations.literal: When Tang forces pressed on Luoyang, Shichong sent envoys begging Jiande for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang armies closed on Luoyang, Shichong sent envoys begging Jiande for help.

sentences.zh: 建德中書侍郎劉彬說建德曰；

translations.literal: Jiande's vice minister of the central secretariat Liu Bin urged Jiande, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin, vice minister of the central secretariat under Jiande, argued to him:

sentences.zh: 「天下大亂，唐得關西，鄭得河南，夏得河北，共成鼎足之勢。

translations.literal: "The realm is in great disorder: Tang holds the western passes, Zheng holds the Henan heartland, and Xia holds Hebei—they stand like the three legs of a tripod.
translations.idiomatic: "The empire is shattered. Tang holds the western passes, Zheng the heart of Henan, Xia Hebei—three powers like the legs of a tripod.

sentences.zh: 今唐舉兵臨鄭，自秋涉冬，唐兵日增，鄭地日蹙，唐強鄭弱，勢必不支。

translations.literal: Now Tang has raised arms against Zheng; from autumn through winter Tang forces have grown daily while Zheng territory has shrunk daily—Tang strong, Zheng weak—the outcome cannot be in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tang has marched on Zheng. From autumn into winter Tang's armies have swelled while Zheng's lands have shrunk. Tang grows stronger, Zheng weaker—the end is plain.

sentences.zh: 鄭亡，則夏不能獨立矣。

translations.literal: If Zheng falls, Xia cannot stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: If Zheng falls, Xia cannot stand alone.

sentences.zh: 不如解仇除忿，發兵救之，夏擊其外，鄭攻其內，破唐必矣。

translations.literal: Better to set aside old grudges, send troops to save them: Xia strikes from without, Zheng attacks from within, and Tang will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Better bury the feud and send relief: Xia strikes from without, Zheng from within—Tang will surely break.

sentences.zh: 唐師既退，徐觀其變，若鄭可取則取之，並二國之兵，乘唐師之老，天下可取也。

translations.literal: Once Tang's army withdraws, watch how matters develop at leisure—if Zheng can be taken, take it; unite the forces of both states, strike while Tang's army is worn, and the realm can be seized.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang withdraws, watch and wait. If Zheng can be swallowed, swallow it. Unite both armies, strike when Tang is spent, and all under heaven may yet be yours.

sentences.zh: 」建德從之，遣使詣世充，許以赴援。

translations.literal: Jiande agreed, sent envoys to Shichong, and promised to come to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande took his counsel, sent envoys to Shichong, and promised to march to his rescue.

sentences.zh: 又遣其禮部侍郎李大師等詣唐，請罷洛陽之兵，秦王世民留之，不答。

translations.literal: He also sent his vice minister of rites Li Dashii and others to Tang to ask that the Luoyang campaign be halted; the Prince of Qin, Shimin, detained them and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Li Dashii of the ministry of rites and others to Tang, asking that the siege of Luoyang be lifted. The Prince of Qin, Shimin, kept them and made no answer.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛卯，王世充許、亳等十一州皆請降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinmao, Shichong's eleven prefectures including Xu and Bo all petitioned to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day xinmao, eleven of Wang Shichong's prefectures—including Xu and Bo—petitioned to surrender.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，燕郡王李藝又擊竇建德軍於籠火城，破之。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, the Prince of Yan Commandery, Li Yi, again struck Dou Jiande's army at Longhuo Fortress and routed it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen, Li Yi, Prince of Yan Commandery, again smashed Dou Jiande's army at Longhuo Fortress.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，王世充隨州總管徐毅舉州降。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Wang Shichong's Suizhou commander Xu Yi surrendered the whole prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinchou, Xu Yi, Wang Shichong's commander at Suizhou, brought the entire prefecture over.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，峽州剌史許紹攻蕭銑荊門鎮，拔之。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Xia Prefecture governor Xu Shao attacked Xiao Xian's Jingmen garrison and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Xu Shao, governor of Xia Prefecture, stormed Xiao Xian's garrison at Jingmen and took it.

sentences.zh: 紹所部與梁、鄭鄰接，二境得紹士卒，皆殺之，紹得二境士卒，皆資給遣之。

translations.literal: Shao's territory bordered Liang and Zheng; when his two neighbors captured his soldiers, they all killed them—but when Shao captured soldiers from their territories, he supplied them and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's command marched alongside Liang and Zheng. When those two realms captured his men, they killed them. When Shao captured theirs, he fed them, paid their way, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 敵人愧感，不復侵掠，境內以安。

translations.literal: The enemy were shamed and moved; they no longer raided, and the borderlands were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies were shamed into gratitude and stopped raiding; within his borders there was peace.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑遣其齊王張繡攻長沙，董景珍謂繡曰：「『前年醢彭越，往年殺韓信』，卿不見之乎？

translations.literal: Xiao Xian sent his Prince of Qi, Zhang Xiu, to attack Changsha; Dong Jingzhen said to Xiu, "Have you not seen how 'the year before last they minced Peng Yue, and last year they killed Han Xin'?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian sent his Prince of Qi, Zhang Xiu, against Changsha. Dong Jingzhen said to him, "Have you forgotten? 'The year before last they minced Peng Yue; last year they killed Han Xin.'

sentences.zh: 何為相攻！

translations.literal: Why attack each other!
translations.idiomatic: Why turn our blades on one another!

sentences.zh: 」繡不應，進兵圍之。

translations.literal: Xiu did not answer and advanced to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu made no reply and pressed on to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 景珍欲潰圍走，為麾下所殺；

translations.literal: Jingzhen tried to break out and flee but was killed by his subordinates;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen tried to break out and escape, but his own men cut him down;

sentences.zh: 銑以繡為尚書令。

translations.literal: Xian made Xiu director of the department of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian made Zhang Xiu director of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 繡恃功驕橫，銑又殺之。

translations.literal: Xiu, relying on merit, grew arrogant and overbearing; Xian killed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu, drunk on his victory, grew insolent—and Xiao Xian killed him too.

sentences.zh: 由是功臣諸將皆有離心，兵勢益弱。

translations.literal: From this the meritorious ministers and generals all lost heart, and military strength grew weaker.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the great captains and ministers lost heart, and Xia's armies grew ever feebler.

sentences.zh: 王世充遣其兄子代王琬、長孫安世詣竇建德報聘，且乞師。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong sent his elder brother's son, the Prince Substitute Wan, and Zhangsun Anshi to Jiande on a return embassy—and to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his nephew, Prince Wan, and Zhangsun Anshi to Jiande on a return embassy—and to plead for an army.

sentences.zh: 突厥倫特勒在并州，大為民患，并州總管劉世讓設策擒之。

translations.literal: The Turk Illi Teler was at Bing Prefecture, greatly harming the people; Bing Prefecture commander Liu Shirang devised a plan and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk Illi Teler was ravaging Bing Prefecture. Liu Shirang, the prefectural commander, laid a trap and took him.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，甚喜。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted when he heard.

sentences.zh: 張道源從竇建德在河南，密遣人詣長安，請出兵攻洺州以震山東。

translations.literal: Zhang Daoyuan was with Dou Jiande in Henan and secretly sent men to Chang'an asking that troops be sent to attack Ming Prefecture and shake the east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daoyuan, then with Dou Jiande in Henan, secretly sent men to Chang'an urging a strike on Ming Prefecture to shake the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔世讓為行軍總管，使將兵出土門，趣洺州。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, an edict made Shirang campaign commander and ordered him to lead troops out of Tumen and march on Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu the court made Shirang campaign commander and ordered him out through Tumen Pass toward Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己酉，瓜州刺史賀拔行威執驃騎將軍達奚暠，舉兵反。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Guazhou governor Heba Xingwei seized Flying-Cavalry General Daxi Gao and rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou, Heba Xingwei, governor of Guazhou, seized Flying-Cavalry General Daxi Gao and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 是歲，李子通渡江攻沈法興，取京口。

translations.literal: That year Li Zitong crossed the Yangtze to attack Shen Faxiing and took Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Zitong crossed the Yangtze against Shen Faxiing and seized Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 法興遣其僕射蔣元超拒之，戰於庱亭，元超敗死，法興棄毘陵，奔吳郡。

translations.literal: Faxiing sent his vice director Jiang Yuanchao to resist; they fought at Chiting—Yuanchao was defeated and killed; Faxiing abandoned Piling and fled to Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Faxiing sent his vice director Jiang Yuanchao to meet him. They fought at Chiting; Yuanchao was beaten and killed. Faxiing abandoned Piling and fled to Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是丹楊、毘陵等郡皆降於子通。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commanderies of Danyang and Piling all surrendered to Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang, Piling, and the surrounding commanderies all submitted to Zitong.

sentences.zh: 子通以法興府掾李百藥為內史侍郎、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Zitong appointed Li Baiyao, a staff officer from Faxiing's former administration, as vice minister of the central secretariat and director of the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong took Li Baiyao, once a clerk in Faxiing's administration, and made him vice minister of the central secretariat and director of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 杜伏威遣行臺左僕射輔公祏將卒數千攻子通，以將軍闞稜、王雄誕為副。

translations.literal: Du Fuwei sent his itinerant secretariat vice director Fu Gongshi with several thousand troops to attack Zitong, with generals Kan Ling and Wang Xiongdan as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei sent Fu Gongshi, vice director of his itinerant secretariat, with several thousand men against Zitong, backed by Generals Kan Ling and Wang Xiongdan.

sentences.zh: 公祐渡江攻丹楊，克之，進屯溧水，子通帥眾數萬拒之。

translations.literal: Gongshi crossed the river, attacked Danyang, and took it; he advanced and encamped at Lishui, and Zitong led tens of thousands to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi crossed the river, stormed Danyang, and pushed on to camp at Lishui. Zitong marched out with tens of thousands to block him.

sentences.zh: 公祐簡精甲千人，執長刀為前鋒；

translations.literal: Gongshi selected a thousand picked armored men and armed them with long swords as vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi picked a thousand elite armored men, armed them with long swords, and placed them in the van;

sentences.zh: 又使千人踵其後，曰：「有退者即斬之。

translations.literal: He also placed a thousand men behind them, saying, "Whoever retreats will be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He posted another thousand behind them with the order: "Any man who falls back dies.

sentences.zh: 」自帥餘眾，復居其後。

translations.literal: He personally led the remaining troops and took position still farther back.
translations.idiomatic: He himself led the rest of the army and took up position still farther to the rear.

sentences.zh: 子通為方陳而前，公祐前鋒千人殊死戰，公祐復張左右翼以擊之，子通敗走，公祐逐之，反為所敗，還，閉壁不出。

translations.literal: Zitong advanced in square formation; Gongshi's thousand-man vanguard fought to the death; Gongshi then extended left and right wings to strike—Zitong was routed and fled; Gongshi pursued but was in turn defeated, withdrew, and shut the gates without coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong came on in a square formation. Gongshi's thousand-man van fought as if death meant nothing; then he spread left and right wings and struck. Zitong broke and ran. Gongshi chased him—but was beaten in turn, pulled back, and shut himself behind his walls.

sentences.zh: 王雄誕曰：「子通無壁壘，又狃於初勝，乘其無備擊之，可破也。

translations.literal: Wang Xiongdan said, "Zitong has no fortifications and is emboldened by his first victory—strike him while he is unprepared and he can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiongdan said, "Zitong has no walls to hide behind, and he is drunk on his first victory. Hit him while he is careless and he will break.

sentences.zh: 」公祐不從。

translations.literal: Gongshi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi refused.

sentences.zh: 雄誕以其私屬數百人夜出擊之，因風縱火，子通大敗，降其卒數千人。

translations.literal: Xiongdan led several hundred of his own followers out by night to attack; taking advantage of the wind, they set fires—Zitong was utterly defeated and thousands of his soldiers surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiongdan led several hundred of his own household troops out in a raid. They rode the wind to set fires. Zitong was routed, and thousands of his men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 子通食盡，棄江都，保京口，江西之地盡入於伏威，伏威徙居丹楊。

translations.literal: Zitong's provisions were exhausted; he abandoned Jiangdu, held Jingkou, and all the lands west of the river fell to Fuwei, who moved his seat to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong's grain ran out. He abandoned Jiangdu for Jingkou. All the country west of the river passed to Fuwei, who moved his capital to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 子通復東走太湖，收合亡散，得二萬人，襲沈法興於吳郡，大破之。

translations.literal: Zitong fled east again to Lake Tai, gathered scattered fugitives, mustered twenty thousand men, and raided Shen Faxiing at Wu Prefecture, routing him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong fled east to Lake Tai, gathered the scattered remnants, and raised twenty thousand men. He fell on Shen Faxiing at Wu Prefecture and broke him utterly.

sentences.zh: 法興帥左右數百人棄城走，吳郡賊帥聞人遂安遣其將葉孝辯迎之，法興中塗而悔，欲殺孝辯，更向會稽。

translations.literal: Faxiing fled the city with several hundred close followers; Wu Prefecture bandit chief Wen Ren Sui'an sent his general Ye Xiaobian to welcome him—midway Faxiing repented and wished to kill Xiaobian, then turned toward Kuaiji instead.
translations.idiomatic: Faxiing fled the city with a few hundred followers. Wen Ren Sui'an, a bandit chief of Wu Prefecture, sent Ye Xiaobian to receive him. Midway Faxiing changed his mind, meant to kill Xiaobian, and turned toward Kuaiji instead.

sentences.zh: 孝辯覺之，法興窘迫，赴江溺死。

translations.literal: Xiaobian discovered this; hard pressed, Faxiing threw himself into the river and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobian saw through him. Cornered, Faxiing threw himself into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 子通軍勢復振，帥其群臣徙都餘杭，盡收法興之地，北自太湖，南至嶺，東包會稽，西距宣城，皆有之。

translations.literal: Zitong's armies revived; he led his ministers to move the capital to Yuhang, fully recovered Faxiing's territory—from Lake Tai in the north, the mountain ranges in the south, Kuaiji in the east, and Xuancheng in the west, he held it all.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong's strength returned. He moved his court to Yuhang and swallowed Faxiing's old domain—from Lake Tai in the north to the southern ranges, from Kuaiji in the east to Xuancheng in the west.

sentences.zh: 廣、新二州賊帥高法澄、沈寶徹殺隋官，據州，附於林士弘，漢陽太守馮盎擊破之。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs Gao Facheng and Shen Baoche of Guang and Xin prefectures killed Sui officials, seized the prefectures, and submitted to Lin Shihong; Hanyang grand administrator Feng Ang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Facheng and Shen Baoche, bandit chiefs of Guang and Xin, killed the Sui officials, seized both prefectures, and submitted to Lin Shihong. Feng Ang, grand administrator of Hanyang, crushed them.

sentences.zh: 既而寶徹兄子智臣復聚兵於新州，盎引兵擊之。

translations.literal: Later Baoche's nephew Zhichen regathered troops at Xin Prefecture; Ang led troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Later Baoche's nephew Zhichen raised troops again in Xin Prefecture, and Ang marched against him.

sentences.zh: 戰始合，盎免冑大呼曰：「爾識我乎？

translations.literal: As battle was joined, Ang removed his helmet and shouted, "Do you know me?
translations.idiomatic: As the lines met, Ang tore off his helmet and roared, "Do you know who I am?

sentences.zh: 」賊多棄仗肉袒而拜，遂潰，擒寶徹、智臣等，嶺外遂定。

translations.literal: Many rebels threw down their weapons, bared their torsos, and prostrated themselves; they collapsed; Baoche, Zhichen, and others were captured, and the lands beyond the ranges were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Many rebels dropped their weapons, bared their chests, and kowtowed. The army melted away. Ang seized Baoche, Zhichen, and the rest, and the lands beyond the ranges were pacified.

sentences.zh: 竇建德行臺尚書令恆山胡大恩請降。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande's itinerant secretariat chief minister, the Hun Hu Daen of Hengshan, asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Daen of Hengshan, chief minister on Dou Jiande's itinerant secretariat, offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸酉，以大恩為代州總管，封定襄郡王，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, on the day guiyou, Daen was made commander of Dai Prefecture, enfeoffed as Prince of Dingxiang Commandery, and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day guiyou, the court made Daen commander of Dai Prefecture, created him Prince of Dingxiang Commandery, and granted him the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 代州石嶺之北，自劉武周之亂，寇盜充斥，大恩徙鎮雁門，討擊，悉平之。

translations.literal: North of the Stone Ridge in Dai Prefecture, since Liu Wuzhou's rebellion bandits had swarmed everywhere; Daen moved his seat to Yanmen and hunted them down until all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Stone Ridge in Dai Prefecture, ever since Liu Wuzhou's revolt, bandits had overrun the country. Daen moved his headquarters to Yanmen and hunted them until the region was quiet.

sentences.zh: 稽胡酋帥劉屳成部落數萬，為邊寇；

translations.literal: The Ji Hu chieftain Liu Xiancheng commanded a tribal host of tens of thousands and raided the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiancheng, a Ji Hu chieftain at the head of a tribal host tens of thousands strong, raided the borderlands;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔太子建成統諸軍討之。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, an edict ordered the Crown Prince Jiancheng to take overall command of the armies and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi the court ordered Crown Prince Jiancheng to take command of all armies and crush him.

sentences.zh: 王世充梁州總管程嘉會以所部來降。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's Liang Prefecture commander Cheng Jiahui brought his command over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jiahui, Wang Shichong's commander at Liang Prefecture, defected with his entire force.

sentences.zh: 杜伏威遣其將陳正通、徐紹宗帥精兵二千，來會秦王世民擊王世充，甲申，攻梁，克之。

translations.literal: Du Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with two thousand picked troops to join the Prince of Qin, Shimin, in attacking Wang Shichong; on the day jiashen they attacked Liang Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei sent Generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with two thousand elite troops to join the Prince of Qin against Wang Shichong. On the day jiashen they stormed Liang Prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，黔州刺史田世康攻蕭銑五州、四鎮，皆克之。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Qian Prefecture governor Tian Shikang attacked five prefectures and four garrisons of Xiao Xian and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu, Tian Shikang, governor of Qian Prefecture, attacked five prefectures and four garrisons held by Xiao Xian and took them all.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民選精銳千餘騎，皆皁衣玄甲，分為左右隊，使秦叔寶、程知節、尉遲敬德、翟長孫分將之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Shimin, selected more than a thousand picked horsemen, all in black robes and dark armor, divided into left and right companies, and had Qin Shubao, Cheng Yaojie, Yuchi Jingde, and Zhai Changsun lead them respectively.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin chose more than a thousand crack horsemen, all in black tunics and dark armor, split them into left and right wings, and put Qin Shubao, Cheng Yaojie, Yuchi Jingde, and Zhai Changsun in command.

sentences.zh: 每戰，世民親被玄甲帥之為前鋒，乘機進擊，所向無不摧破，敵人畏之。

translations.literal: In every battle Shimin personally donned dark armor and led them as vanguard; seizing opportunity he pressed the attack—wherever they turned nothing stood unbroken; the enemy feared them.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight Shimin himself put on dark armor and rode at their head. He struck when the moment opened, and nothing in his path held. His enemies learned to fear that black-clad vanguard.

sentences.zh: 行臺僕射屈突通、贊皇公竇軌將兵按行營屯，猝與王世充遇，戰不利。

translations.literal: Itinerant secretariat vice director Qu Tu Tong and Duke of Zanhuang Dou Gui were leading troops to inspect camp encampments when they suddenly encountered Wang Shichong—the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Tong, vice director of the itinerant secretariat, and Dou Gui, Duke of Zanhuang, were making the rounds of the camps when they ran headlong into Wang Shichong and were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民帥玄甲救之，世充大敗，獲其騎將葛彥璋，俘斬六千餘人，世充遁歸。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Shimin, led the dark armor to the rescue; Shichong was utterly defeated; they captured his cavalry general Ge Yanzhang, killed or captured more than six thousand, and Shichong fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin swept in with his dark-armored riders. Shichong was shattered. They took his cavalry general Ge Yanzhang, killed or captured more than six thousand men, and Shichong fled for home.

sentences.zh: 李靖說趙郡王孝恭以取蕭銑十策，孝恭上之。

translations.literal: Li Jing expounded to the Prince of Zhao Commandery, Xiaogong, ten strategies for taking Xiao Xian; Xiaogong submitted them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing laid out for Prince Xiaogong of Zhao Commandery ten plans for bringing down Xiao Xian, and Xiaogong forwarded them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，改信州為夔州，以孝恭為總管，使大造舟艦，習水戰。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinmao, Xin Prefecture was renamed Kui Prefecture; Xiaogong was made commander and ordered to build warships on a large scale and drill in river warfare.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day xinmao, Xin Prefecture was renamed Kui Prefecture. Xiaogong was made its commander and ordered to build a fleet and train his men for river fighting.

sentences.zh: 以孝恭未更軍旅，以靖為行軍總管，兼孝恭長史，委以軍事。

translations.literal: Because Xiaogong had no prior military experience, Li Jing was made campaign commander and concurrently Xiaogong's chief administrator, with military affairs entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiaogong had never commanded in the field, Li Jing was made campaign commander and chief administrator on his staff, with full charge of the war.

sentences.zh: 靖說孝恭悉召巴、蜀酋長子弟，量才授任，置之左右，外示引擢，實以為質。

translations.literal: Li Jing urged Xiaogong to summon the sons and younger brothers of Ba and Shu tribal chiefs, assign posts according to talent, and keep them at hand—outwardly to promote them, in fact as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing urged Xiaogong to summon the sons and younger brothers of the Ba and Shu chieftains, give them posts suited to their gifts, and keep them close—ostensibly as promotions, in truth as hostages.

sentences.zh: 王世充太子玄應將兵數千人，自虎牢運糧入洛陽，秦王世民遣將軍李君羨邀擊，大破之，玄應僅以身免。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's crown prince Xuanying led several thousand troops transporting grain from Hulao into Luoyang; the Prince of Qin, Shimin, sent General Li Junxian to intercept and rout them; Xuanying barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's crown prince Xuanying was escorting several thousand men with grain convoys from Hulao into Luoyang. The Prince of Qin sent General Li Junxian to ambush him, broke the column utterly, and Xuanying escaped with only his life.

sentences.zh: 世民使宇文士及奏請進圍東都，上謂士及曰：「歸語爾王：今取洛陽，止欲息兵。

translations.literal: Shimin sent Yuwen Shiji to memorialize asking to advance the siege of the eastern capital; the Emperor told Shiji, "Go tell your prince: in taking Luoyang now, we mean only to still the weapons of war.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin sent Yuwen Shiji to memorialize for a tighter siege of the eastern capital. The Emperor told him, "Go back and tell your prince: we take Luoyang now only to end the killing.

sentences.zh: 克城之日，乘輿法物，圖籍器械，非私家所須者，委汝收之。

translations.literal: On the day the city falls, imperial regalia, maps and registers, and equipment—not what a private house needs—are entrusted to you for collection.
translations.idiomatic: When the city falls, the imperial regalia, the maps and registers, the engines of state—nothing a private household would keep—are yours to gather in.

sentences.zh: 其餘子女玉帛，並以分賜將士。

translations.literal: The rest—children, silk, and jade—shall all be divided and bestowed upon the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The rest—the people, the silks, the treasure—is yours to divide among the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，世民移軍青城宮，壁壘未立，王世充帥眾二萬自方諸門出，憑故馬坊垣塹，臨谷水以拒唐兵，諸將皆懼。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Shimin moved his army to Qingcheng Palace; the palisades were not yet established when Wang Shichong led twenty thousand men out through Fangzhu Gate, relying on the old horse-park walls and ditches, facing Gushui to resist the Tang army—the generals all feared.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Shimin shifted his camp to Qingcheng Palace. Before his defenses were finished, Wang Shichong led twenty thousand men out through Fangzhu Gate, lining the old horse-park ramparts above the Gushui stream to block the Tang advance. The Tang generals were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 世民以精騎陳於北邙，登魏宣武陵以望之，謂左右曰：「賊勢窘矣，悉眾而出，徼幸一戰，今日破之，後不敢復出矣！

translations.literal: Shimin arrayed elite cavalry on Mount Beimang, climbed Wei Xuandi's tomb mound to look upon them, and said to those around him: "The bandits' strength is exhausted; they have brought out their entire force, gambling on one battle—defeat them today and they will not dare come out again!"
translations.idiomatic: Shimin posted his finest horsemen on Mount Beimang and climbed the tomb mound of Wei Emperor Xuandi to study the enemy. He told his staff, "Shichong is at the end of his rope—he has emptied the city hoping for one decisive fight. Break him today, and he will never risk another sortie."

sentences.zh: 」命屈突通帥步卒五千渡水擊之，戒通曰：「兵交則縱煙。

translations.literal: " He ordered Qu Tu Tong to lead five thousand infantry across the water to attack them, warning Tong: "When the armies engage, raise smoke."
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Qu Tu Tong to take five thousand foot soldiers across the stream and strike, telling him, "When the lines meet, signal with smoke."

sentences.zh: 」煙作，世民引騎南下，身先士卒，與通合勢力戰。

translations.literal: " When the smoke rose, Shimin led his cavalry south, taking the lead before his troops, and joining with Tong's force fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: " As soon as the smoke went up, Shimin spurred his cavalry south at the head of the charge and joined Qu Tu Tong in a pitched fight.

sentences.zh: 世民欲知世充陳厚薄，與精騎數十沖之，直出其背，眾皆披靡，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Shimin wished to know the thickness of Shichong's formation; with several dozen elite horsemen he charged through, going straight out behind their rear—the enemy all scattered, casualties very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to gauge the depth of Shichong's line, Shimin plunged through with a few dozen picked riders and burst out behind the enemy rear. The formation crumbled; casualties were heavy.

sentences.zh: 既而限以長堤，與諸騎相失，將軍丘行恭獨從世民，世充數騎追及之，世民馬中流矢而斃。

translations.literal: Then, blocked by a long embankment, he lost contact with the other horsemen; General Qiu Xinggong alone accompanied Shimin. Several of Shichong's riders caught up—Shimin's horse took an arrow in flight and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: A long dike cut him off from his riders; only General Qiu Xinggong stayed at his side. Shichong's horsemen overtook them, and an arrow brought down Shimin's mount.

sentences.zh: 行恭回騎射追者，發無不中，追者不敢前。

translations.literal: Xinggong turned his horse and shot at the pursuers—every arrow struck its mark, and the pursuers dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong wheeled about and shot down every pursuer in range; none dared press closer.

sentences.zh: 乃下馬以授世民，行恭於馬前步執長刀，距躍大呼，斬數人，突陳而出，得入大軍。

translations.literal: He thereupon dismounted and gave the horse to Shimin; Xinggong, walking ahead of the horse wielding a long blade, leaping and shouting, cut down several men, broke through the formation, and rejoined the main army.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and put Shimin in the saddle, then on foot before the horse, swinging a long saber with leaps and shouts, cut down several foes and fought clear back to the main body.

sentences.zh: 世充亦帥眾殊死戰，散而復合者數四，自辰至午，世充兵始退。

translations.literal: Shichong also led his forces in a desperate battle; they broke and re-formed four times; from the hour of chen to the hour of wu, Shichong's troops at last withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's men fought with desperate fury, rallying and breaking four times over. Not until the hour of wu did they finally give ground.

sentences.zh: 世民縱兵乘之，直抵城下，俘斬七千人，遂圍之。

translations.literal: Shimin unleashed his troops to pursue, reaching straight to the city walls; seven thousand were captured or killed, and he then besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin pressed the pursuit to the walls, killing or capturing seven thousand men, and tightened the siege.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍段志玄與世充兵力戰，深入，馬倒，為世充兵所擒，兩騎夾持其髻，將渡洛水，志玄踴身而奮，二人俱墜馬。

translations.literal: Flying Cavalry General Duan Zhixuan fought fiercely with Shichong's troops, going deep; his horse fell and he was seized by Shichong's soldiers—two horsemen gripped his topknot and were about to cross the Luo River when Zhixuan leapt up with a burst of strength; all three fell from their horses.
translations.idiomatic: Flying Cavalry General Duan Zhixuan fought deep into the Zheng line until his horse went down and enemy soldiers seized him. Two riders grabbed him by the hair to drag him across the Luo, but Zhixuan surged upward and all three tumbled from their saddles.

sentences.zh: 志玄馳歸，追者數百騎，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Zhixuan galloped back; several hundred pursuers did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan rode clear to safety; though hundreds gave chase, none dared close the distance.

sentences.zh: 初，驃騎將軍王懷文為唐軍斥候，為世充所獲，世充欲慰悅之，引置左右。

translations.literal: Earlier, Flying Cavalry General Wang Huaiwen had served as a Tang scout and was captured by Shichong; Shichong wished to win him over and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Tang scout officer Wang Huaiwen had been taken prisoner. Shichong meant to win him over and kept him close at hand.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，世充出右掖門，臨洛水為陳，懷文忽引槊刺世充，世充衷甲，槊折不能入，左右猝出不意，皆愕眙不知所為。

translations.literal: On renyin, Shichong went out through the Right Flank Gate and formed battle lines facing the Luo River; Huaiwen suddenly thrust a spear at Shichong. Shichong wore armor beneath his robes—the spear broke without penetrating. His attendants, taken utterly by surprise, stared in shock, uncertain what to do.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Shichong marched out through the Right Flank Gate and drew up along the Luo. Huaiwen suddenly drove his spear at him. Shichong wore hidden mail—the shaft snapped without piercing—and his startled attendants stood frozen, unsure how to react.

sentences.zh: 懷文走趣唐軍，至寫口，追獲，殺之。

translations.literal: Huaiwen fled toward the Tang army; at Xiekou he was overtaken and captured, then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen bolted for the Tang lines but was run down at Xiekou and executed.

sentences.zh: 世充歸，解去衷甲，袒示群臣曰：「懷文以槊刺我，卒不能傷，豈非天所命乎！

translations.literal: Shichong returned, removed his concealed armor, bared himself before the assembled ministers, and said: "Huaiwen thrust a spear at me and in the end could not wound me—is this not Heaven's mandate!"
translations.idiomatic: Back in the palace, Shichong stripped off his hidden armor and showed himself bare-chested to the court. "Huaiwen drove a spear at me and could not so much as scratch me," he declared. "Is that not Heaven's own decree?"

sentences.zh: 先是，御史大夫鄭頲不樂仕世充，多稱疾不預事，至是謂世充曰：「臣聞佛有金剛不壞身，陛下真是也！

translations.literal: Before this, Grand Censor Zheng Ting had been unwilling to serve Shichong and often pleaded illness to avoid affairs; on this occasion he said to Shichong: "Your subject has heard that the Buddha has a vajra body that cannot be destroyed—Your Majesty truly is such a one!"
translations.idiomatic: For some time Grand Censor Zheng Ting had loathed serving Shichong and kept pleading illness to avoid office. Now he told him, "I hear the Buddha's body is diamond-hard and indestructible—Your Majesty, you truly are that man!"

sentences.zh: 臣實多幸，得生佛世，願棄官削髮為沙門，服勤精進，以資陛下之神武。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly most fortunate to be born in the age of a Buddha; I wish to abandon office, shave my head, and become a monk, serving diligently in religious practice to augment Your Majesty's divine martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: How fortunate I am to live in the age of a living buddha! I beg leave to resign, shave my head, and take the tonsure, dedicating my devotions to Your Majesty's godlike valor.

sentences.zh: 」世充曰：「國之大臣，聲望素重，一旦入道，將駭物聽。

translations.literal: " Shichong said: "A great minister of state, your reputation has long been weighty—if you suddenly enter the Way, it will startle all observers."
translations.idiomatic: " Shichong replied, "You are a pillar of the realm, a man of great standing. If you suddenly renounce the world, you will shock everyone who hears of it.

sentences.zh: 俟兵革休息，當從公志。

translations.literal: Wait until arms and war have rested, then I shall follow your wish.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the fighting is over, and I will honor your wish.

sentences.zh: 」頲固請，不許。

translations.literal: " Ting insistently petitioned; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Ting pressed his request again; Shichong refused.

sentences.zh: 退謂其妻曰：「吾束髮從官，志慕名節，不幸遭遇亂世，流離至此，側身猜忌之朝，累足危亡之地，智力淺薄，無以自全。

translations.literal: He withdrew and said to his wife: "From youth I entered office, aspiring to reputation and integrity; unhappily I met a chaotic age and was cast adrift here, standing sideways in a court of suspicion, feet tangled in a place of peril—my wit and strength are shallow; I cannot preserve myself."
translations.idiomatic: At home he told his wife, "I took up office young, caring for honor and principle. Fate dropped me into this chaos and this suspicious court on the brink of ruin. I am not clever enough to save myself.

sentences.zh: 人生會當有死，早晚何殊？

translations.literal: Human life must end in death—what difference between sooner and later?
translations.idiomatic: Every life ends in death—what matter whether it comes sooner or later?

sentences.zh: 姑從吾所好，死亦無憾！

translations.literal: For now let me follow what I prefer—even in death there will be no regret!
translations.idiomatic: Let me at least do as I wish; I will have no regrets even in death.

sentences.zh: 」遂削髮被僧服。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he shaved his head and put on monk's robes.
translations.idiomatic: " He shaved his head and donned the monk's robe.

sentences.zh: 世充聞之，大怒曰：「爾以我為必敗，欲苟免邪？

translations.literal: Shichong heard of this and said in great anger: "Do you take me as certain to be defeated, wishing to slip away and save yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong heard, he flew into a rage. "You think I am doomed and want to save your own skin, do you?

sentences.zh: 不誅之，何以制眾！

translations.literal: If I do not execute him, how shall I control the multitude!
translations.idiomatic: If I do not kill you, how can I keep the rest in line?

sentences.zh: 」遂斬頲於市。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beheaded Ting in the market.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Ting beheaded in public.

sentences.zh: 頲言笑自若，觀者壯之。

translations.literal: Ting spoke and smiled as if at ease; onlookers found him admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Ting met death smiling and unafraid; the crowd admired his composure.

sentences.zh: 詔贈王懷文上柱國、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously conferred on Wang Huaiwen the rank of Shangzhuguo and made him governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Wang Huaiwen a Supreme Pillar of the State and governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 并州安撫使唐儉密奏：「真鄉公李仲文與妖僧志覺有謀反語，又娶陶氏之女以應桃李之謠。

translations.literal: Bingzhou Pacification Commissioner Tang Jian secretly memorialized: "Duke of Zhenxiang Li Zhongwen had seditious words with the sorcerer-monk Zhijue, and also took a daughter of the Tao clan to fulfill the prophecy of 'peach and plum.'"
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou Pacification Commissioner Tang Jian secretly reported that Duke of Zhenxiang Li Zhongwen had spoken of rebellion with the rogue monk Zhijue and had married a daughter of the Tao clan to fulfill the omen that "peaches and plums" would rise.

sentences.zh: 諂事可汗，甚得其意，可汗許立為南面可汗。

translations.literal: Flattering and serving the Qaghan, he greatly pleased him; the Qaghan promised to establish him as Southern Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: He had fawned on the Qaghan and won his favor; the Qaghan had even promised to set him up as khan of the south.

sentences.zh: 及在并州，贓賄狼藉。

translations.literal: Moreover while in Bingzhou, bribes and corruption lay strewn everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In Bingzhou his corruption was flagrant.

sentences.zh: 」上命裴寂、陳叔達、蕭瑀雜鞠之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered Pei Ji, Chen Shuda, and Xiao Yu jointly to investigate and try him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor ordered Pei Ji, Chen Shuda, and Xiao Yu to examine the case jointly.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，仲文伏誅。

translations.literal: On yisi, Zhongwen was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Li Zhongwen was executed.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，王泰棄河陽走，其將趙敻等以城來降。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Wang Tai abandoned Heyang and fled; his generals Zhao Xiong and others surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Wang Tai abandoned Heyang and fled; his officers Zhao Xiong and others surrendered the city to Tang.

sentences.zh: 別將單雄信、裴孝達與總管王君廓相持於洛口，秦王世民帥步騎五千援之，至轘轅，雄信等遁去，君廓追敗之。

translations.literal: Separate generals Shan Xiongxin and Pei Xiaoda were locked in stalemate with Defender-in-Chief Wang Junguo at Luokou; the Prince of Qin, Shimin, led five thousand infantry and cavalry to reinforce them; reaching Hulao, Xiongxin and the others fled; Junguo pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng generals Shan Xiongxin and Pei Xiaoda were trading blows with Tang defender Wang Junguo at Luokou. The Prince of Qin hurried five thousand men to his aid. Near Hulao, Shan and Pei broke off and fled; Junguo pursued and routed them.

sentences.zh: 壬子，延州總管段德操擊劉屳成，破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On renzi, Yanzhou Defender-in-Chief Duan Decao attacked Liu Zhancheng, defeated him, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Yanzhou defender Duan Decao smashed Liu Zhancheng's force and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，王世充懷州刺史陸善宗以城降。

translations.literal: On yimao, Wang Shichong's Huai Prefecture governor Lu Shanzong surrendered his city.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Lu Shanzong, Wang Shichong's governor of Huai Prefecture, surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 秦王世民圍洛陽宮城，城中守禦甚嚴，大砲飛石重五十斤，擲二百步，八弓弩箭如車輻，鏃如巨斧，射五百步。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Shimin, besieged Luoyang's palace city; the city's defenses were exceedingly strict—great catapults hurled stones weighing fifty jin two hundred paces; eight-bow crossbows fired bolts like cart-wheel spokes, arrowheads like great axes, shooting five hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin tightened the siege of Luoyang's inner palace city. The defenders were formidably armed: catapults flung fifty-jin stones two hundred paces; great crossbows shot bolts thick as wheel spokes and heads wide as axes five hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 世民四面攻之，晝夜不息，旬餘不克。

translations.literal: Shimin attacked on all four sides day and night without cease; after more than ten days he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin assaulted from every side without pause, day and night, but after ten days and more had not broken the walls.

sentences.zh: 城中欲翻城者凡十三輩，皆不果發而死。

translations.literal: Within the city thirteen groups wished to turn traitor and open the gates; none succeeded in acting and all died.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen separate parties inside the city plotted to open the gates; every plot was crushed before it could act, and the plotters were killed.

sentences.zh: 唐將士皆疲弊思歸，總管劉弘基等請班師。

translations.literal: Tang officers and soldiers were all exhausted and weary, thinking of returning; Defender-in-Chief Liu Hongji and others requested withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang army was worn down and homesick; defender Liu Hongji and others asked to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 世民曰：「今大舉而來，當一勞永逸。

translations.literal: Shimin said: "Having come on a great expedition, we ought to toil once and rest forever."
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said, "We came in force to settle this once for all.

sentences.zh: 東方諸州已望風款服，唯洛陽孤城，勢不能久，功在垂成，奈何棄之而去！

translations.literal: The eastern provinces have already submitted at the mere sight of our banners; only Luoyang stands alone—its strength cannot last long, success is within reach—how can we abandon it and leave!
translations.idiomatic: The eastern provinces have already bowed before us; Luoyang is a lone citadel that cannot hold out. Victory is in sight—how can we throw it away and march off?

sentences.zh: 」乃下令軍中曰：「洛陽未破，師必不還，敢言班師者斬！

translations.literal: " He thereupon issued orders through the army: "Luoyang unbroken, the army will certainly not return; whoever dares speak of withdrawal shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the army: "Until Luoyang falls, no one returns. Speak of retreat, and you die.

sentences.zh: 」眾乃不敢復言。

translations.literal: " The troops then dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: " No one ventured another word.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，亦密敕世民使還，世民表稱洛陽必可克，又遣參謀軍事封德彝入朝面論形勢。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of this and also secretly ordered Shimin to return; Shimin memorialized saying Luoyang could certainly be taken, and further sent Staff Officer Feng Deyi to court to argue the situation in person.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and secretly ordered Shimin home. Shimin replied by memorial that Luoyang would fall, and sent his staff officer Feng Deyi to court to argue the case in person.

sentences.zh: 德彝言於上曰：「世充得地雖多，率皆羈屬，號令所行，唯洛陽一城而已，智盡力窮，克在朝夕。

translations.literal: Deyi said to the Emperor: "Although Shichong holds much territory, it is mostly in loose subordination; his orders reach only Luoyang city itself—wits and strength are exhausted; its capture is a matter of days."
translations.idiomatic: Feng told the Emperor, "Shichong's domain looks vast, but most of it pays him only nominal obedience. Only Luoyang truly obeys him. He is spent; the city will fall within days.

sentences.zh: 今若旋師，賊勢復振，更相連接，後必難圖！

translations.literal: If we now turn back, the bandits' power will revive again, reconnect with one another, and afterward will surely be hard to overcome!
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw now and the enemy will rally, link up again, and grow far harder to defeat.

sentences.zh: 」上乃從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 世民遣世充書，諭以禍福；

translations.literal: Shimin sent Shichong a letter, expounding fortune and calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin wrote to Shichong, urging him to weigh ruin against reward;

sentences.zh: 世充不報。

translations.literal: Shichong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong did not answer.

sentences.zh: 戊午，王世充鄭州司兵沈悅遣使詣左武候大將軍李世勣請降。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Wang Shichong's Zheng Prefecture Army Controller Shen Yue sent envoys to Left Martial Guard General Li Shiji to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Shen Yue, Wang Shichong's army controller at Zhengzhou, sent envoys to Li Shiji asking to surrender.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍王群廓夜引兵襲虎牢，悅為內應，遂拔之，獲其荊王行本及長史戴冑。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Wang Qunkuo by night led troops to assault Hubao; Yue served as inside contact, and they took it, capturing the Prince of Jing Xingben and Chief Administrator Dai Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Wang Qunkuo struck Tiger Lock Fortress by night with Shen Yue as his inside man. They took the fort and captured Prince of Jing Xingben and chief administrator Dai Zhou.

sentences.zh: 悅，君理之孫也。

translations.literal: Yue was the grandson of Junli.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue was a grandson of Shen Junli.

sentences.zh: 竇建德克周橋，虜孟海公。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande captured Zhouqiao and took Meng Haigong prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande seized Zhouqiao and captured Meng Haigong.
